title: Schedule of Fees, the Fair Company
author: S. Marr, Captain; entered by the Company's clerk
body:
# Schedule of Fees

*Protection of the person and goods on the south shore road, Pennyfold to the Stride's Foot, by writ, sealed and witnessed. All fees at a fair price.*

---

**A traveller on foot**, per mile: one penny. *With a pack*, two.

**A cart**, per wheel per mile: a mark. *A cart that has been protected before*, the same. We do not reward the forgetful.

**A bolt of cloth off the Bleaching Green**, per week, against the green's writ: one bolt. *Not the dyed. The Circle's white, where there is any.*

**A laundress**, per crossing: nothing. *Captain's order. Anyone who asks a laundress for a fee answers to the Captain, who will read him the writ he signed.*

**A traveller who declines protection**: nothing, and none.

---

*In the Captain's hand, at the foot:* Everything on this page is in the Charter of 998 if you read it slowly. The Tallymen wrote every word of it. I have only charged for it.

title: Words, and What They Fetch
author: A. Quell
body:
# Stock

*A slate from the ledge in the deepest hall, chalked in a clerk's hand. The prices are rubbed out and written again often.*

---

**A quiet dog.** Eight marks. Lasts the night. *Not on the Lamp's dogs; they were bred to it.*

**A cold lock.** Twenty. Opens nothing; makes the lock forget it was shut. *Tallymen's strongrooms: forty, and I choose the night.*

**Footsteps.** Twelve a night, the whole street. *Lantern Row has asked for a season. No.*

**A boat's oars.** Six. *To Gullhithe men, eight. They talk.*

**A net's knots**, so a Mere boat sees a Mere net: four a net. *The Sedgish tie better than we do and it shows. See to it.*

---

*Under a line, not rubbed out:* **A name that does not carry.** Not for sale.

*Under that, smaller:* They taught it us last, on the Spire, and said never to use it on a living man. I have never sold it. I have used it twice.

title: The Warm-Egg Board
author: the egg-collectors of Gullhithe, many hands
body:
# The warm eggs

*A board wedged in a crack of the vault, knife-cut, a line a spring. The oldest lines are worn nearly smooth.*

---

*Year of the long frost.* One warm. Took it home in my shirt. It hatched. We drowned it. **Hesper.**

*Next spring.* One warm. Left it. **Hesper.**

*Two springs after.* One warm, from the room with nothing in it. Brought it up for the Lamp's keeper to look at. He said to put it back where it was and not to come down here again. **Wat Gannet.**

*The spring after.* Came down again. **Wat Gannet.**

*No year.* Did not come up. *(In another hand:)* Wat.

---

*The last line, fresh-cut:* The floor is warm down here. Warm as a hearth. Something's been lying on it. **O.G.**

title: Letters to the Row, Unsent
author: Crispin Tolley, clerk to the Tallymen at the Counting Tower
body:
# To the Steward of the Row

*A bundle of letters in a clerk's hand, each addressed, each sealed, none sent, tied with ledger-tape and weighted with a stone on the tower's step.*

---

*The first.* Sir. I beg to be relieved of the Counting Tower. No cart has come down the North Road owing the tax of 942 in my time or my predecessor's, and the tower is cold. **C. Tolley.**

*The ninth.* Sir. The ledger is being kept. I do not keep it. I sit at the window every hour of light, as the post requires, and nothing comes down the road, and when I turn the page the page is full. **C. Tolley.**

*The fortieth.* Sir. The figures are the Builders'. I have learned to read them from the lamp-posts on the Stride. They are counting carts. They are counting carts that have not come yet. There are a great many of them and they are all coming down this road. I have stopped counting. I have not stopped sitting at the window. **C.T.**

*The last, unsealed:* Whoever reads this, do not send it. The Row would send another clerk.

title: A Receipt for Brass
author: unsigned; a Tallymen's receipt-form
body:
# Received

*A printed Tallymen's receipt, the kind given for a fine paid at the charter-board, filled in by hand and pushed into the crack of the Charter Stone where a pin was drawn.*

---

**Received of:** the Charter Stone.

**The sum of:** one pin, brass, the third of seven.

**Being:** the price of the North Road's peace, the third instalment.

**Witnessed:** by nobody, which the Charter allows between midnight and the first cart.

---

*On the back, in a different hand, in charcoal:* The clans broke it in 712 and the Tallymen pinned it so each side could say the other had done the breaking. We are only taking back what was paid for it. When the last pin is out it will be what it was before anybody agreed to anything, and then we will see who comes to swear.

title: The Masons' Lintel, Copied Fair
author: copied for the Quiet Hands; the copyist's mark is a closed hand
body:
# The lintel at Pellow's house

*A fair copy on good paper, the cutting reproduced line for line, and the copyist's notes in the margin.*

---

HOB ASHWORTH, SETTER. 40 DAYS.
NED ASHWORTH, SETTER. 40 DAYS.
WILL CRESS, CARVER. 55 DAYS, AND THE STAIR.
MOLL TAMSELL, BANKER. 38 DAYS.
THE BOY, CARRYING. 40 DAYS. *NO NAME GIVEN; he was the boy.*
NOT PAID. BUILDING IS NOW A SERVICE. SO IS THIS.

---

*In the margin:* Two hundred and thirteen days of work at the old rate, with a hundred and three years of interest at the Row's own rate for a debt unpaid, is a sum larger than Guildmaster Pellow's house, his guild, and the Row it sits on. The Hands do not intend to collect it. The Hands intend that the Tallymen should know it has been copied.

title: Bowl-Signals, for the Undercroft Run
author: unsigned; a smuggler's crib
body:
# When the bowl is lit

*A crib on oiled cloth, folded small, kept under a stone at the beacon's foot.*

---

**One fire, steady.** A boat tonight. Come under the Lamp's turning, not across it.

**One fire, covered and shown three times.** No boat. The Tallymen are on the Stride.

**Two fires.** The Hole is full. Go to the Undercroft direct and ask for the door.

**No fire.** The serpent. *Somebody has added this in a different hand and nobody has rubbed it out.*

---

*At the foot:* Do not ring the bowl. It is a bell, turned over, and it remembers. Ambrose says it can be heard at the Spire if it is rung, and the Circle will come to see who rang it, and so will the other thing.

title: A Smoker's Note on the Third Arch
author: Berrit, smoker, of Merrowhithe
body:
# The drip

*Pinned to the third arch's pier with a fish-hook, above a bucket.*

---

Whoever is walking the channel along the top: the water you are walking in is coming down on my pike. I have moved the racks twice. It follows the racks.

I have measured it. A bucket a day at the third arch, half at the fourth, a cupful at the fifth, and none at the broken end, where it would be pouring out if it were rain. It is not rain. It tastes of stone and it is cold, colder than the Mere in the spring, colder than anything that has been out in the sun.

Nobody alive has seen water in this channel. My grandmother said the Builders built it to bring something down off the fell. If that is so, then something up there has started to send it again, and I would like to know what my fish are hanging under before I sell them.

*Under it, in a Sayer's neat hand:* Measured also. Agreed. Do not drink it. **I.O.**

title: The Slades' Thousand-Book
author: Barnet Slade, and his father, and his
body:
# Down to the landing

*A quarry-book with a slate cover, kept on the splitting-bench. One line a thousand.*

---

*Grandfather's hand.* A thousand, blue, for the Row's new roof. A thousand, blue. A thousand, grey, for the Sayers' outbuildings, and they paid in advance, which frightened him.

*Father's hand.* A thousand, blue. A thousand, blue. Boatman says nine hundred. Post says a thousand. Post is right.

*Barnet's hand.* A thousand, blue. Half a thousand, and then we hit the black. It will not split. Nothing will cut it. Slate off the face against it splits sweet as you like and hums in your hand for a day after.

*Barnet's hand, later.* Put one aside. Jessamy says it hums the same note the horn at the Listening Post was built to hear. I said the Sayers can come and hear it then. She said the Sayers never come to anybody; somebody has to go to them.

title: Writ of Protection, the Bleaching Green
author: the Fair Company; witnessed
body:
# Writ of Protection

*Printed on good paper with the Tallymen's old seal at its head, filled in by hand, and nailed to the bleachers' hut.*

---

Be it known that the Bleaching Green, its frames, its cloth and its keeper **Linnet Whitlow** are under the protection of the **Fair Company** of Pennyfold, against all harm from any quarter but the Company's, for so long as the fee is paid.

**The fee:** one bolt a week, at the Company's choosing.

**Witnessed:** *a name that has been scraped off and a new one written over it.*

**Sealed:** S. Marr, Captain.

---

*Written under it in chalk, in a bleacher's big hand:* The Circle's white. They chose the Circle's white. Answerable for every ell.

title: A Writ, Torn Across
author: the Fair Company
body:
# Writ of Protection

*Torn across and dropped by the gate, the halves still pinned together with a thorn.*

---

The bearer, **a carter of Sedgehithe, name not given**, and his cart of two wheels, are under the protection of the Fair Company from Pennyfold to the Stride's Foot, *for this crossing only*.

**The fee:** eleven marks. **Paid:** *nine.*

---

*In the Captain's hand, across the tear:* Nine is not eleven. The charter does not say protection may be paid in part. It does not say protection may be withdrawn in part either, so I have withdrawn all of it, and the Company has read him the writ, and he has gone home the long way, and so has his cart, separately.

title: A First Primer of the Hush
author: the Sayers' Circle, for the use of first-year clerks; annotated by A. Quell
body:
# The Hush: a first primer

*The Spire's own printing. Every word has a price pencilled beside it.*

---

**I. Of silence.** A silence is not an absence. It is a thing said the other way, and it must be said as carefully. *(Margin: eight marks.)*

**II. Of the small words.** The latch, the dog, the stair. A first-year clerk may say these in the Spire's hearing and nowhere else. *(Margin: the latch, twenty. The dog, eight. The stair, twelve. Nowhere else: ha.)*

**III. Of carrying.** A word carries as far as it is known. A name carries as far as it is spoken. The Circle's first duty is that no name be Hushed, since a name that does not carry is a person who does not either. *(Margin, heavily: not for sale.)*

---

*The last page, where the fourth lesson should be, has been torn out. Along the tear, in pencil:* Kept back. Sold to nobody. Used twice. The Circle should be unsaid for teaching it, and I with it, for learning it so well.

title: Chalked on the Hinge-less Door
author: Merrowhithe's egg-collectors
body:
# On the black jamb, at shoulder height

*Chalk on the Builders' stone, which does not take chalk well: every mark has been gone over many times, a spring at a time.*

---

GANNET. *A gannet drawn, badly.*

ONE A NEST, NEVER THE LAST.

IF IT'S WARM LEAVE IT.

*Under that, crossed out and written again, and crossed out:* IF IT'S WARM BRING IT UP FOR THE KEEPER.

*Lower, a child's hand:* WAT WENT IN HERE.

*Lowest, fresh, in a hand that pressed hard enough to break the chalk:* So did I. It's warm at the bottom. Something's been lying there longer than any of us. **O.G.**
